verdicts.note: Use another letter for the scalar (for example c) instead of a, because linear-network and subset-network bind a as the bank index (a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)) and the scalar meaning does not hold there.

Use another letter for the linear map (for example L) instead of T, because linear-network and subset-network bind T as a three-element subset of [h]; the linear map is not used under that name on those pages.
Do not bind S as a separate letter for the inverse; write the inverse as T^{-1} as the rest of the page does, because linear-network and subset-network bind S as a three-element subset of [h].

Use vertex letters that are not vector letters from linear-algebra (for example p and q, so that the frame is D_p and edges run from p to q), since the frame page's v names a vertex and linear-algebra's v names a vector in V.
Use another vertex letter for the edge start (for example p in place of u), because linear-algebra binds u as an arbitrary vector in V and the frame page's u names a vertex.
